blocks.heading: Entry points
lines: Start with fixed positions: an end, the middle seat, a seat number.
Next use 'immediately next to' and 'opposite' clues.
Keep 'not next to' and 'somewhere to the left' clues for last.

blocks.heading: Draw it
lines: Row: write seat numbers 1 to n from the left and fill them in.
Circle: draw n dots, fix one person to remove rotations, number the seats clockwise.
When a clue allows two places, draw one row or circle for each case.
Keep a second detail, such as a job or city, in a small table under the diagram.

blocks.heading: Left and right
lines: In a row facing the same way, left and right are the same for everyone.
Facing the centre of a round table: left is clockwise, right is anticlockwise, seen from above.
Facing outward, it is the other way round.
'Second to the left' means two seats along, with one seat skipped.

blocks.heading: Common traps
lines: Three seats apart means two people between.
A circle wraps around: the last seat is next to the first.
Dropping a case too early. Test every clue on each case.
A condition inside a question ('If X sits at an end') holds for that question only.
